Dear Hiring Team,

I am writing to apply for the 2026 PRC Internship & Practicum. As a graduate student pursuing a Master of Arts in Clinical Mental Health Counseling (CACREP) at Liberty University, I am eager to gain supervised clinical experience in dual-diagnosis and co-occurring disorder treatment and to grow within a team that values compassion, accountability, professionalism, and teamwork. I would be honored to bring these values to either the adult PHP/IOP program or the Adolescent Wellness Academy, whichever placement best fits your team's current needs.

My coursework and clinical training have prepared me to contribute meaningfully to your program. Through classes in Ethical and Legal Issues in Counseling, Counseling Techniques and the Helping Relationship, Assessment Techniques in Counseling, and Psychopathology, I have built a strong foundation in case conceptualization, biopsychosocial assessment, and clinical documentation. I am also familiar with several of the evidence-based modalities used across PRC's programs, including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, and I bring additional grounding in trauma-informed care through my completion of Trust-Based Relational Intervention (TBRI) and Emotional, Physical, Intellectual, and Character-based needs (EPIC) training.

During my full-semester practicum with 4KIDS of South Florida, Inc., I worked directly with a vulnerable population, applying reflective listening, empathy, and trauma-informed approaches while maintaining clear, ethical professional boundaries and HIPAA compliance. In my roles as an Ascent Mentor, Fish Group Leader, and Camp Counselor, I have consistently built trust and rapport with individuals from diverse backgrounds, navigated emotionally challenging conversations with care, and adapted my approach to meet each person where they are — skills I look forward to applying to individual, family, and group therapy, whether working with adults or adolescents facing mental health and substance use challenges.
I am especially drawn to PRC's integration of relapse prevention strategies, crisis intervention and safety planning, and stabilization approaches within a supportive, high-standards clinical environment, as well as the family-centered, judgment-free care that defines the Adolescent Wellness Academy. My goal for this practicum is to build hands-on skill in treatment planning, evidence-based interventions such as CBT and DBT, and family involvement, while growing into a more confident and ethical clinician under the guidance of your licensed supervisors. I understand this is an unpaid clinical training placement and am fully prepared to complete a Level 2 background check and drug test prior to placement.

Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to PRC's mission of helping clients and their families on the path to recovery, in whichever program best fits your current placement needs.

Sincerely,

Kate Melendy McCool

My goal moving forward is to grow into a compassionate, skilled clinician who can walk alongside people during some of their hardest moments and help them find real healing.

Ultimately, I want to leave this practicum with a clearer, more confident clinical identity, shaped by PRC's values of compassion, accountability, professionalism, and teamwork

questionnaire.text: What do you hope to learn and gain from this experience?
questionnaire.response: Beyond specific clinical skills, I hope this experience teaches me what it actually looks like to sit with people in crisis and walk alongside them through recovery — not just in theory, but in real time, under real supervision. I want to learn how experienced clinicians make decisions in the moment, how they balance structure with flexibility, and how they hold professional boundaries while still showing up with genuine warmth. I also hope to learn more about myself as a future counselor: where my strengths already show up, where I still need to grow, and how I handle the emotional weight of this work over time. I'd love to leave this practicum not just more skilled, but more self-aware and more confident in who I am as a clinician.
